rules.title: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (JCO): just cause required, relocation assistance for no-fault evictions
rules.requirement: If you rent in Los Angeles in a unit not covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance and have lived there at least six months (or your original lease has expired), your landlord can evict you only for a listed at-fault or no-fault reason. For no-fault reasons, such as an owner move-in, demolition or removal from the rental market, the landlord may have to pay you relocation assistance.
rules.key_value: Just cause required after 6 months' tenancy or lease expiration; relocation assistance for no-fault evictions

coverage.summary: Most residential rental properties in the City of Los Angeles not regulated by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance, including buildings newer than October 1, 1978 and single-family dwellings. Applies once the tenant has lived in the unit at least six months or the original lease has expired, whichever comes first.
minor_exemptions_not_in_data: some non-profit homeless facilities or short-term substance abuse treatment centers
some properties owned by HACLA or the government

rules.exemptions: Units under the RSO (covered separately); transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity/sorority houses, owner's roommate, certain cooperatives, some non-profit homeless or treatment facilities, some HACLA or government properties. Tenancies under six months whose original lease has not expired.
rules.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.
rules.interaction: Covers units not regulated by the City's RSO. Single-family homes and condos exempt from state AB 1482 may still be covered by the JCO.

rules.title: No eviction for nonpayment unless arrears exceed Fair Market Rent
rules.requirement: In Los Angeles RSO and JCO units, your landlord cannot evict you for falling behind on rent unless you owe more than one month's Fair Market Rent for your unit's bedroom size.
rules.key_value: Arrears must exceed the Fair Market Rent (FMR) for the unit's bedroom size

coverage.summary: All RSO and JCO rental units in the City of Los Angeles.

rules.citation: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (JCO) / Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO)
rules.quoted_span: Effective March 27, 2023, landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes an amount higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR).

rules.title: Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (AB 1482) statewide rent cap
rules.requirement: If your unit is more than 15 years old and not under local rent control, annual rent increases are capped at 5% plus regional inflation, or 10%, whichever is lower. In Los Angeles the maximum was 8.9% for August 1, 2024 to July 31, 2025.

coverage.summary: Residential units more than 15 years old (rolling), excluding units subject to local rent control (LA RSO), deed-restricted affordable units, certain dormitories, owner-occupied duplexes, and individually owned single-family homes and condos with proper written notice.
minor_exemptions_not_in_data: units deed-restricted to low or moderate income households
single-family homes and condominiums not owned by a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member, with written notice to tenant

rules.exemptions: Units built within the last 15 years (rolling); deed-restricted affordable units; certain dormitories; two-unit property where owner occupied the other unit for the entire tenancy; individually owned single-family homes/condos with written notice (not where another dwelling unit is on the lot); units subject to the City's RSO.
rules.citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12 (AB 1482, Tenant Protection Act of 2019)
rules.quoted_span: nual rent increases are limited to no more than 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living for the region in which the property is located, or 10% whichever is lower).
rules.interaction: Does not apply to units already subject to the Los Angeles RSO. Effective date not stated on this page; the rolling-exemption example implies the law applied as of January 1, 2020.
